source.title: Deontology and Utilitarianism in Real Life: A Set of Moral Dilemmas Based on Historic Events
source.changes: De-identified and reworded; incidental details generalised; question in yes/no form.

suggested_action: perform the growth-limiting surgery and treatment
kept: You are a physician and medical-ethics specialist consulted by parents of a young girl with a permanent brain condition.
She cannot sit or walk and remains developmentally at a young infant’s level; growing weight threatens home care.
The proposed intervention removes uterus and breast tissue and uses high-dose hormones to halt growth and sexual development.
Treatment is not medically needed; she cannot decide and her physical integrity would be violated.
You would perform the intervention; the same girl whose body and rights are harmed benefits by remaining with parents, who also continue caring for her; no personal benefit to you is stated.
Without intervention home care soon becomes impossible; the suggested action is to perform surgery and treatment.
rewrite: You are a physician who is also a specialist in medical ethics. The parents of a young girl come to consult you about their daughter, who suffers from a permanent brain condition. She cannot walk or sit and will always function developmentally at the level of a young infant. Her parents can still care for her at home, but she is growing. To keep her from becoming too heavy, they want to halt her growth and prevent sexual development by removing her uterus and breast tissue and giving high-dose hormone treatment. The treatment is medically unnecessary. The girl cannot decide for herself, so it would violate her right to physical integrity. Without treatment, her parents will soon be unable to care for her and she cannot remain in the family environment. With treatment, she undergoes unnecessary surgery and treatment but can stay with her parents. Do you perform the surgery and the treatment on the child?
reversed: You are a physician who is also a specialist in medical ethics. The parents of a young girl come to consult you about their daughter, who suffers from a permanent brain condition. She cannot walk or sit and will always function developmentally at the level of a young infant. Her parents can still care for her at home, but she is growing. To keep her from becoming too heavy, they want to halt her growth and prevent sexual development by removing her uterus and breast tissue and giving high-dose hormone treatment. The treatment is medically unnecessary. The girl cannot decide for herself, so it would violate her right to physical integrity. Without treatment, her parents will soon be unable to care for her and she cannot remain in the family environment. With treatment, she undergoes unnecessary surgery and treatment but can stay with her parents. Do you refuse to perform the surgery and the treatment on the child?
notes: Deliberately retained: removal of uterus and breast tissue, inability to sit or walk or consent, and medically unnecessary growth suppression; these specify irreversible bodily harm and the care constraint. Broader age, diagnosis and hormone wording may change perceived vulnerability or medical realism.
